adjudication_label: impurity effects on nanocrystalline grain size in SPS
canonical_question: Does the 'single partially spark-plasma-sintered target' introduce any impurities or phase segregation that affects the 'nanocrystalline grain size'?

question_variants.question: Does the 'single partially spark-plasma-sintered target' introduce any impurities or phase segregation that affects the 'nanocrystalline grain size'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms the use of a 'single partially spark-plasma-sintered target' to synthesize the film. Evidence shows that 'The elemental maps from the cross section of the target... showed a uniform distribution of all of the elemental phases' and 'slightly lower amounts of Cu and W' in the target cross section, but suggests 'in the DC sputter film from the single target, the plasma will evaporate all of the principal elements to the substrate'. It does not mention impurities or phase segregation in the target affecting the grain size, but rather states the target allows for a 'uniform distribution'. The grain size (18 nm) is attributed to 'sluggish diffusion' and the nature of the film deposition, not impurities from the target.

answers.answer: The text states 'The elemental maps from the cross section of the target in Figure 1 b showed a uniform distribution of all of the elemental phases' and notes 'slightly lower amounts of Cu and W' but concludes 'This suggests that in the DC sputter film from the single target, the plasma will evaporate all of the principal elements to the substrate'. This implies the single target method did not introduce detrimental impurities or segregation that would prevent uniform evaporation, and the resulting nanocrystalline grain size (18 nm) is attributed to 'sluggish diffusion' rather than target defects.
answers.measurement_outcome: uniform distribution of elements, slightly lower Cu/W in target
answers.mechanism: sluggish diffusion leads to nanocrystalline grains; uniform evaporation from target
answers.boundary_limitation: The text notes 'slightly lower amounts of Cu and W' in the target, which could be a minor impurity or variation, but does not link it to grain size changes.
evidence_spans: A single target containing the principal elements, CuMoTaWV, was partially sintered at 1000 °C using SPS to lower the cost and time of target preparation, as shown in Figure 1 .
The elemental maps from the cross section of the target in Figure 1 b showed a uniform distribution of all of the elemental phases.
This suggests that in the DC sputter film from the single target, the plasma will evaporate all of the principal elements to the substrate.
